longTitle.officialTitle: To prevent the termination of the temporary office of bankruptcy judges in certain judicial districts.

main.enactingFormula: Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled,

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This Act may be cited as the “Temporary Bankruptcy Judgeships Extension Act of 2012”.

section.heading: EXTENSION OF TEMPORARY OFFICE OF BANKRUPTCY JUDGES IN CERTAIN JUDICIAL DISTRICTS.

subsection.heading: Temporary Office of Bankruptcy Judges Authorized by Public Law 109-8.—

paragraph.heading: Extensions.—
paragraph.chapeau: The temporary office of bankruptcy judges authorized for the following districts by section 1223(b) of Public Law 109-8 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) are extended until the applicable vacancy specified in paragraph (2) in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the respective district occurs:

subparagraph.content: The northern district of New York.
The eastern district of North Carolina.

subparagraph.heading: Single vacancies.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Except as provided in subparagraphs (B), (C), (D), (E), (F), (G), and (H), the 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for each district specified in paragraph (1)—

clause.content: occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: Central district of california.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st, 2d, and 3d vacancies in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the central district of California—

clause.content: occurring 5 years or more after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: District of delaware.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st, 2d, 3d, and 4th vacancies in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the district of Delaware—

clause.content: in the case of the 1st and 2d vacancies, occurring more than 6 years after the date of the enactment of this Act,
in the case of the 3d and 4th vacancies, occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: Southern district of florida.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st and 2d vacancies in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the southern district of Florida—

clause.content: occurring more than 6 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: District of maryland.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st, 2d, and 3d vacancies in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the district of Maryland—

clause.content: occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: Eastern district of michigan.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the eastern district of Michigan—

clause.content: occurring 6 years or more after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge, shall not be filled.

subparagraph.heading: District of puerto rico.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the district of Puerto Rico—

clause.content: occurring 6 years or more after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge, shall not be filled.

subparagraph.heading: Eastern district of virginia.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the eastern district of Virginia—

clause.content: occurring 6 years or more after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge, shall not be filled.

paragraph.heading: Applicability of other provisions.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), all other provisions of section 1223(b) of Public Law 109-8 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) remain applicable to the temporary office of bankruptcy judges referred to in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Temporary Office of Bankruptcy Judges Extended by Public Law 109-8.—

paragraph.heading: Extensions.—
paragraph.content: The temporary office of bankruptcy judges authorized by section 3 of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 1992 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) and extended by section 1223(c) of Public Law 109-8 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) for the district of Delaware, the district of Puerto Rico, and the eastern district of Tennessee are extended until the applicable vacancy specified in paragraph (2) in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the respective district occurs.

subparagraph.heading: District of delaware.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 5th vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the district of Delaware—

clause.content: occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: District of puerto rico.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 2d vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the district of Puerto Rico—

clause.content: occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

subparagraph.heading: Eastern district of tennessee.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the eastern district of Tennessee—

clause.content: occurring more than 9 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

paragraph.heading: Applicability of other provisions.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), all other provisions of section 3 of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 1992 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) and section 1223(c) of Public Law 109-8 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) remain applicable to the temporary office of bankruptcy judges referred to in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Temporary Office of the Bankruptcy Judge Authorized by Public Law 102-361 for the Middle District of North Carolina.—

paragraph.heading: Extension.—
paragraph.content: The temporary office of the bankruptcy judge authorized by section 3 of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 1992 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) for the middle district of North Carolina is extended until the vacancy specified in paragraph (2) occurs.

paragraph.heading: Vacancy.—
paragraph.chapeau: The 1st vacancy in the office of a bankruptcy judge for the middle district of North Carolina—

subparagraph.content: occurring more than 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, and
resulting from the death, retirement, resignation, or removal of a bankruptcy judge,

paragraph.heading: Applicability of other provisions.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), all other provisions of section 3 of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 1992 (28 U.S.C. 152 note) remain applicable to the temporary office of the bankruptcy judge referred to in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Bankruptcy Filing Fees.—
subsection.content: Section 1930(a)(3) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking “$1,000” and inserting “$1,167”.

subsection.heading: United States Trustee System Fund.—
subsection.content: Section 589a(b)(2) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking “55” and inserting “48.89”.

subsection.heading: Collection and Deposit of Miscellaneous Bankruptcy Fees.—
subsection.content: Section 406(b) of the Judiciary Appropriations Act, 1990 (28 U.S.C. 1931 note) is amended by striking “25” and inserting “33.33”.

subsection.heading: Paygo Offset Expenditure Limitation.—
subsection.content: $42 of the incremental amounts collected by reason of the enactment of subsection (a) shall be deposited in a special fund in the Treasury to be established after the date of enactment of this Act. Such amounts shall be available for the purposes specified in section 1931(a) of title 28, United States Code, but only to the extent specifically appropriated by an Act of Congress enacted after the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.heading: Effective Date.—
subsection.content: This section and the amendments made by this section shall take effect 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.heading: SUBSEQUENT REAUTHORIZATION.
section.content: Prior to further reauthorization of any judgeship authorized by this Act, the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate and House of Representatives shall conduct a review of the bankruptcy judgeships authorized by this Act to determine the need, if any, for continued reauthorization of each judgeship, to evaluate any changes in all bankruptcy case filings and their effect, if any, on filing fee revenue, and to require the Administrative Office of the Courts to submit a report to the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate and House of Representatives on bankruptcy case workload, bankruptcy judgeship costs, and filing fee revenue.
